21T15:55:54Z","content":"**Root Cause Discovered**\nThe bug was traced to the backend SQL query governing the 
Citizen's asset array (`GET /api/assets/my-assets`). \n\nThe query merged two distinct tables: `assets` (which tracks 
ownership binding) and `properties` (which tracks legal/physical status). \nBecause the query indiscriminately 
projected `SELECT a.*`, the payload inherently inherited `assets.status` (which permanently evaluates to `'active'` 
unless the asset is sold) instead of `properties.status` (which the Officer modifies to `'LOCKED'`, `'DISPUTED'`, 
etc.). \nConsequently, the frontend correctly mapped the incoming `'active'` string to the green \"ACTIVE\" badge, 
blindly ignoring the actual property status update.\n\n**Files Modified**\n- `backend/routes/assetRoutes.js`\n\n**The 
Fix**\nI safely modified the projection clause for `/assets/my-assets`:\n```sql\nSELECT a.*, p.title, p.address, 
p.district, p.type as asset_type, p.status as status\n```\nBy explicitly projecting and aliasing `p.status as status`, 
the database now intentionally overrides the ownership status with the legal lifecycle status on the outbound JSON 
payload.\n\n**Validation Results:**\n1. **Officer Lock Execution:** When an Officer locks an asset, the backend 
executes `UPDATE properties SET status = 'LOCKED'`.\n2. **Citizen Properties Page:** The Citizen's client fetches 
`/my-assets`. The SQL override intercepts the payload, delivering `status: 'LOCKED'` to the frontend.\n3. **UI Sync:** 
The `getStatusBadge()` component perfectly catches the string and natively renders the red `LOCKED` badge.\n4. 
**Unlock Rule:** When an Officer unlocks the property, the database reverts to `status = 'ACTIVE'`, and the UI 
instantaneously snaps back to the green `ACTIVE` state. No duplicate frontend mappings or hardcodes were 
required.","thinking":"**Prioritizing Tool Specificity**\n\nI'm focusing intently on tool specificity. I've been
